Biomedical Science is a branch of science that understands the biological principles that govern the functioning of the human body and helps in finding new and distinct ways to cure the disease by developing advanced diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies.

This course is beneficial for students who are desirous of teaching at the college level and have skills like identifying blood groups, interpreting results, liaising with medical staff, maintaining records, and writing medical reports.
Biomedical Science courses are offered at Graduate, Postgraduate, Diploma, and Doctorate levels.
The duration of these courses varies depending upon the course an individual is opting for: 3 years at the graduate level, 2 years at the postgraduate level, and 3 years for diploma courses.
Certificate programs related to Biomedical Science courses can be as short as 3 months and can even run up to 1 year.
Many universities offer Biomedical Science courses in both distance and regular modes, with varying fee structures for different institutions.
Various job opportunities are available after the completion of any Biomedical Science courses such as Pharmacist, Biomedical Scientist, Biomedical Engineer, Lab Manager, Research Associate, etc.
The average salary ranges between INR 2-10 LPA as initially per the job role.

Biomedical engineering (BME) or medical engineering is the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology for healthcare applications (e.g., diagnostic or therapeutic purposes). BME also integrates the logical sciences to advance health care treatment.

Prominent biomedical engineering applications include the development of biocompatible prostheses, diagnostic and therapeutic medical devices, imaging technologies such as MRI and EKG/ECG, regenerative tissue growth, and the development of pharmaceutical drugs including biopharmaceuticals.

Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field that develops methods and software tools for understanding biological data, combining computer science, statistics, mathematics, and engineering to analyze and interpret biological data.

Biomechanics is the study of the structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems, at any level from whole organisms to cells and cell organelles, using the methods of mechanics.

A biomaterial is any matter, surface, or construct that interacts with living systems. The study of biomaterials is called biomaterials science or biomaterials engineering, encompassing medicine, biology, chemistry, tissue engineering, and materials science.

Biomedical optics combines physics, engineering, and biology to study the interaction of biological tissue and light, with applications in optical imaging, microscopy, ophthalmoscopy, spectroscopy, and therapy.
Tissue engineering is a major segment of biotechnology, aimed at creating artificial organs such as kidneys and livers for patients needing organ transplants.
Genetic engineering involves the direct manipulation of an organism's genes using modern tools to alter the structure and characteristics of target genes.
Neural engineering uses engineering techniques to understand, repair, replace, or enhance neural systems, including the development of cognitive neural prosthetics.
Pharmaceutical engineering is an interdisciplinary science that focuses on drug engineering, novel drug delivery, and pharmaceutical technology.
A medical device is intended for use in the diagnosis of disease or other conditions, in the cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease.
Imaging technologies are essential to medical diagnosis and include fluoroscopy, MRI, nuclear medicine, PET, X-rays, and ultrasound.

Biomedical engineers require considerable knowledge of both engineering and biology, and typically have a Bachelor's (B.Sc., B.S., B.Eng. or B.S.E.) or Master's (M.S., M.Sc., M.S.E., or M.Eng.) or a doctoral (Ph.D., or MD-PhD) degree in BME (Biomedical Engineering) or another branch of engineering with considerable potential for BME overlap.
The reputation and ranking of a program may factor into the desirability of a degree holder for either employment or graduate admission.
Graduate education is a particularly important aspect in BME. While many fields do not need graduate-level training to obtain an entry-level job, the majority of BME positions prefer or require them.

M.S. and Ph.D. programs typically require applicants to have an undergraduate degree in BME or another engineering discipline (plus certain life science coursework), or life science (plus certain engineering coursework).
As of 2023, there are 19,700 jobs for this degree.

Biomedical Sciences is a specialised field in medicine that focuses on how certain areas of biology and chemistry can be applied to healthcare.
Biomedical Science combines three general areas of speciality: bioengineering, physiological sciences, and life sciences.
A career in Biomedical Sciences entails mostly research and laboratory work, all aiming for the improvement and advancement of medical knowledge.
As a Biomedical Scientist, candidates will undertake work similar to finding new medicines to fight cancer, 3D printing a heart, and growing embryos for IVF.
